title: Evidence-linked alternative-protein demand drivers
source_policy: Retained local evidence only; no new retrieval or source-data changes; no original source reproduced in full.
scope: Eight organizing factors, not an exhaustive driver census. Mechanisms and recommendations are hypotheses/proposals unless explicitly classified otherwise.

us_comparison.provenance: Reviewer-supplied comparison prompts; original US-panel passage and executed methods not established in this revision.
us_comparison.restriction: Do not attribute these as verified original-panel findings, pool panels, reproduce private questionnaire text or infer equivalent methods. Umar supplemental US arm is separate.

drivers.direction: Conditional upward mechanism; mixed net demand effect
drivers.mechanism: Purchasing power can expand feasible purchases, but income growth does not identify which foods gain.
drivers.upward_pressure: Higher real resources could support purchases of replacement products.
drivers.obstacle: Income may instead expand conventional animal-food spending; distributional and price differences matter.

india.evidence: Retained WEO real-income path is an input; the spending response is an analyst-selected elasticity.

pakistan.evidence: Retained WEO path and relative-income transfer are used; no national alternative-protein sales anchor validates that response.

drivers.model_treatment: Explicit income index and elasticity; distribution and causal demand elasticity are not estimated.
drivers.signpost: Revisions to real income and actual replacement-food purchases by defined income group.
drivers.obstacle_disposition: Monitor macro revisions and measure segmented purchases.

drivers.direction: Lower comparable prices could increase access; magnitude unmeasured
drivers.mechanism: Retail price per usable serving and household budget jointly constrain purchase.
drivers.upward_pressure: Lower real price per comparable serving could permit more frequent purchase.
drivers.obstacle: Price parity with meat alone may not make a product affordable relative to other foods or household budgets.

india.evidence: SOFI reports 40.4% unable to afford a healthy diet in 2024; this is not an alternative-product premium.

pakistan.evidence: SOFI reports 60.3% unable to afford a healthy diet in 2024; comparable alternative-product price/paid-purchase evidence remains incomplete.
pakistan.evidence_class: Published modelled economic-access estimate plus retained-evidence gap

drivers.model_treatment: No separate retail-price response or price-parity term; possible indirect effects in additional growth are not identified.
drivers.signpost: Dated matched retail price, pack/serving definition, in-stock status, paid purchase and unsubsidized repeat purchase.
drivers.us_theme: Health and R&D are reviewer-supplied prompts; no causal transfer from US sales is assumed.
drivers.obstacle_disposition: Bounded retail audit and purchase study.

drivers.factor: Dietary practice, taste and health perceptions
drivers.direction: Mixed; depends on product, meal and group
drivers.mechanism: A replacement must perform a valued role in actual meals; perceived taste, health and processing can help or impede use.
drivers.upward_pressure: Familiar preparation and satisfactory sensory performance could support repeat use.
drivers.obstacle: An analogue can be irrelevant to a meal or conflict with preferences; health beliefs are not nutritional or clinical findings.

india.evidence: Bryant et al. measure product beliefs and hypothetical intention in an urban/affluent-skewed online sample. GFI estimates a dairy-heavy 2022 category mix.
india.evidence_class: Sample-specific stated intent and external modelled category estimate
india.population: India online respondents n=1,024; separate national market estimate

pakistan.evidence: Animal-protein food-balance supply provides context, not evidence that people will choose chicken or milk replacements. No matched national preference estimate is established here.
pakistan.evidence_class: National supply proxy and retained-evidence gap
pakistan.population: National food availability; not sampled purchasers

drivers.model_treatment: Pakistan animal-supply multiplier; no separate taste, cuisine, health-perception or category-choice model.
drivers.signpost: Meal-specific blind and labelled choices, preparation success and paid repeat use by defined groups.
drivers.us_theme: Health trends: reviewer-supplied comparison prompt; test locally without assuming its direction.
drivers.obstacle_disposition: Study product/meal fit and distinguish perceptions from health evidence.

drivers.mechanism: Familiarity and trusted information may affect willingness, but expressed acceptance need not become purchase.
drivers.upward_pressure: Credible information and appropriate product experience could reduce uncertainty.
drivers.obstacle: Stigma, distrust or unfamiliarity can coexist with favourable hypothetical answers.

india.evidence: Bryant et al. associate familiarity with acceptance in their study; this is not a randomized information effect or a national conversion rate.
india.evidence_class: Observational association in an online intention survey
india.population: India online sample; country comparisons retain recruitment limits

pakistan.evidence: The retained package does not supply a comparable national paid/repeat-purchase measure; India evidence cannot fill it.

drivers.model_treatment: No independently estimated social-legitimacy coefficient; possible residual effects cannot be separated.
drivers.signpost: Clearly separated stated intention, paid first purchase, unsubsidized repeat purchase and conventional-food displacement.
drivers.us_theme: Politics and health: reviewer-supplied prompts, not established country effects.
drivers.obstacle_disposition: Bounded study; no national acceptance ranking.

drivers.direction: Conditional enabling or constraining; not a universal demand effect
drivers.mechanism: A named product needs its relevant assurance and authorization questions resolved separately.
drivers.upward_pressure: A documented applicable route can reduce uncertainty for suppliers and prospective purchasers.
drivers.obstacle: Ingredient/process-specific halal questions and food-authorization requirements cannot be inferred from a general institution.

india.evidence: This bounded source set supplies no product-specific halal determination or novel-product approval for the proposed fermentation example.
india.population: Named product and intended jurisdiction must be specified

pakistan.evidence: The 2016 Act establishes halal institutional provisions; it does not settle a particular fermentation ingredient or product food authorization.
pakistan.population: Act scope; not a product decision or complete current legal audit

drivers.model_treatment: No certification parameter; cultivated meat excluded; fermentation is not separately estimated.
drivers.signpost: Dated written product/process-specific decisions from the relevant competent bodies, recorded separately for assurance and food authorization.
drivers.us_theme: Political environment: reviewer-supplied prompt; US regulatory conclusions are not transferred.
drivers.obstacle_disposition: Obtain qualified product-specific clarification before any pilot sale.

drivers.direction: Potentially supportive or restrictive; uptake effect unmeasured
drivers.mechanism: Policy can alter research resources, market entry and compliance conditions; implementation mediates effects.
drivers.upward_pressure: Implemented support could improve capabilities and feasible product pathways.
drivers.obstacle: An announcement can remain unimplemented or fail to affect consumer price and availability.

india.evidence: BioE3 announcement of 24 August 2024 identifies smart proteins, R&D and Bio-AI/biomanufacturing infrastructure.
india.population: Named policy sectors; not observed firms or buyers

pakistan.evidence: The Halal Authority Act supplies a dated institutional basis; it is not evidence of equivalent smart-protein funding or product uptake.
pakistan.population: Dated legal scope; not programme performance

drivers.model_treatment: No separate policy multiplier; cannot estimate a policy effect from the scenarios.
drivers.signpost: Policy instrument, implementation evidence, disbursement, product authorization and observable retail outcome tracked as different stages.
drivers.us_theme: Political environment: reviewer-supplied prompt pending original-panel provenance.
drivers.obstacle_disposition: Monitor specific implementation stages; do not forecast approvals.

drivers.direction: Conditional upward capacity mechanism; demand and constraints unresolved
drivers.mechanism: Technical capabilities and reliable distribution can improve performance, unit cost and availability.
drivers.upward_pressure: A verified bottleneck resolved through a feasible intervention could improve product access.
drivers.obstacle: Vacancies and company-list entries do not measure productive capacity, skills shortages or repeated retail availability.

india.evidence: GFI talent study reports 20 industry responses and 19 academic participants, with technical skill concerns. Retained job advertisements measure activity only.
india.evidence_class: Sampled employer/academic testimony and job-board proxy
india.population: Study cohorts and covered advertisements; not national workforce

pakistan.evidence: Two directory rows and 58 recorded 2025 vacancies enter the retained proxies; uneven coverage prevents inferring national absence or operating capacity.

drivers.model_treatment: Vacancy CAGR sets India drift ceiling; relative directory/vacancy densities bound Pakistan industry factor. Neither relationship is fitted to sales.
drivers.signpost: Verified facilities/staff, measured process performance, batch/unit cost, outlet availability and repeat purchases; advertisements tracked separately.
drivers.us_theme: R&D landscape: reviewer-supplied prompt; technical bottlenecks require country/product evidence.
drivers.obstacle_disposition: India employer-linked bottleneck trial; Pakistan feasibility first; retail availability audit.

drivers.mechanism: AI might affect technical performance and cost; retail pass-through and improvements in conventional production determine relative competitiveness.
drivers.upward_pressure: Validated process gains could lower delivered costs or improve functionality.
drivers.obstacle: A laboratory or company claim need not survive scale-up or reach retail prices; conventional products may improve too.

india.evidence: BioE3 proposes Bio-AI infrastructure. The retained proxy does not estimate an AI spending effect.
india.population: Policy sectors; no national treatment-effect sample

pakistan.evidence: No independently established country-level AI effect on alternative-protein spending is supplied by this retained package; absence here is not evidence that applications do not exist.

drivers.model_treatment: No separate AI multiplier; avoid adding a bonus already implicit in growth assumptions.
drivers.signpost: AI versus credible non-AI baseline for validated output, cost, consistency and retail price/availability; also observe conventional comparators.
drivers.us_theme: R&D landscape: reviewer-supplied prompt; no universal AI advantage assumed.
drivers.obstacle_disposition: Only a feasible benchmarked technical trial; otherwise monitor.
